Record preliminary Q4 and full-year 2021 — first $100M-plus quarter ($104.3M, +192%) and first $300M-plus year; domestic +238%.
Call dominated by two governance/control disclosures: a non-cash stock-comp error and a 15-day Form 10-K filing extension.

Stock-comp error from misinterpreting a Class 3 modification rule on grants to former foundational employees/retired directors whose awards continued vesting — understating expense ~$3.1M in Q2 and ~$12.1M in Q3 (CFO figures), requiring restatement of those 10-Qs.
Management concluded a material weakness existed in internal controls over financial reporting as of December 31, 2021; remediation in progress.
The SEC investigation remains ongoing with no material developments and is 'completely separate' from the stock-comp error.

Q4 GAAP gross margin fell to 39.9% (from 48.9%) on imported can costs, raw materials, ocean freight (containers near $20,000) and repackaging; expected to persist through Q3 2022 then normalize toward FY2020 levels.
Imported cans carry a ~3-4% margin impact, stemming from a strategic late-2020/early-2021 decision to import cans to fulfill demand.
DSD network grew from 150 partners / 80% coverage at start of 2021 to 276+ service centers / ~98% population coverage; ~65% of MULO+C stores DSD-serviced.
Convenience doors up 95% to ~60,000 (~44% ACV, ~56% runway); Circle K national contract (~6,000 doors); Costco scaled to 561 stores (Q4 +1,100%).
COVID-suppressed 2020 fitness and vending channels rebounded in 2021 (+91% / +186%), contributing ~$14.7M of incremental full-year revenue.
Net inventory rose ~$172.8M to $191.2M to support the six-orbit warehouse model and spring resets, including ~$60-70M of prepaid cans/raw materials.
2022 framed as 'the year of activation' — activating the DSD network, driving distribution and velocity; promotional pricing implemented to offset inflation.
Q4 included an $8-8.5M tax benefit from releasing valuation allowances on prior-year tax losses; tax rate to be significantly higher going forward.
Macro headwinds — aluminum can shortage still tight, labor/trucking shortages, rising gas prices; COVID disrupted the finance team in Jan/early Feb 2022.
Asked to confirm the control issues are exclusively isolated to the stock-based comp accounting as the audit wraps up.
That is the current indication, but cautioned the company is still going through a first-year audit and internal controls are a major remaining aspect — kept 'the door open.'
Shelf-space resets, club expansion & share trajectory
Asked about expected material new placements and club-channel expansion, and where tracked-channel share (~2%) goes over the next 12-36 months.

Scan data extremely strong, velocity still rising even in club (Costco) and Amazon despite broadening distribution. Costco a big 2021 surprise; Sam's Club and BJ's in discussion for 2022. Highlighted the Circle K national agreement (~6,000 stores). Did not commit to a quantified share target.
Asked for directional gross-margin guidance for 2022 and to marry near-term pressure with the longer-term Monster-like EBITDA margin opportunity.

Many variables — local vs. imported can mix (flowing through COGS through Q2 and a bit beyond), freight, oil-price macro pressure (containers near $20,000) — make precise guidance difficult. Once normalized, gross profitability returns toward 2020 levels with EBITDA leverage from volume. Imported cans expected to cycle through ~Q3 2022; pricing/promotional strategies to offset inflation.
Asked whether there is anything beyond the stock-comp issue management is aware of, and whether the error relates to the SEC investigation.

First-year audit with greater scrutiny so something could surface, but at this point nothing of that nature seen — kept 'the door open.' Stock-comp matter is 'not necessarily' related to the SEC investigation — an internal valuation issue on modified awards; management confident in the preliminary numbers.

Asked how the ~10%+ Florida home-state share reconciles with the mid-3s national share, whether anything prevents state share improving, and the state of distribution moving away from Florida; also whether the SEC investigation is separate.

Florida's share reflects nearly two years of full DSD coverage plus Circle K, 7-Eleven and Publix — evidence Celsius performs at or above competitors with the same opportunity. Texas, California and others gaining share as the DSD network builds. CFO firmly confirmed the SEC investigation is 'completely separate' from the stock-comp error.
Circle K rollout & DSD expansion target
Asked about the Circle K contract rollout, the current overall DSD percentage, and a reasonable end-of-FY2022 DSD target.

Circle K is a national rollout into ~6,000 doors with ~4 flavors average — a strong DSD jump-start. 270+ service centers cover ~98% of population; some state gaps remain, with majority coverage and the ability to service all key accounts targeted by end of 2022. 2022 framed as 'all about activation.'
Asked for detail on the six-orbit warehouse model ramp — status, milestones, timeline, and expected benefit once optimized.

Began in Q3 2021 with warehouse buildout and inventory increases; Q4 focused on optimizing inventory and establishing logistics lanes to reduce lead times, drive full-truckload/full-pallet efficiency, and improve freight costs and margins. Expected well optimized by end of Q1 2022.
DSD conversion %, can cost spread & marketing spend
Asked how many accounts are actually converted to DSD, the imported-vs-domestic can cost spread and where margins land, and how to think about marketing/sales spend.

98% is population coverage; ~65% of MULO+C stores currently DSD-serviced. Imported cans carry a ~3-4% margin impact (container costs near $20,000, easing), cycling through ~Q3 2022. Investing ahead of revenue, expects to maintain current spending levels through 2022, with ex-stock-comp G&A at ~6.1%.
Stock comp run rate, tax rate & inventory build

Asked whether all stock-comp is in G&A, whether Q4 stock-comp is a normal run rate, the deferred-tax release amount, the go-forward tax rate, color on the inventory build, and where inventory days land in 12 months.

100% of stock-comp is in G&A; Q4 level roughly the go-forward run rate; deferred-tax release ~$8-8.5M; with remaining NOLs the tax rate will be significantly higher (jurisdiction/profitability dependent). Inventory build includes ~$60-70M of prepaid cans/raw materials for 2022 resets and summer; targeting ~90-120 days on hand (currently above that after large December production runs).
Asked whether anything other than North America focus is constraining international sales and whether the growth rate can accelerate.

Deliberately conservative on international, sees opportunities in the Nordics, UK/Germany Amazon, and Southeast Asia, but methodical as it scales. CFO reiterated the master-distributor model avoids a large footprint and currency exposure.
Asked, given strong Q4 growth and difficult 2H 2022 comparisons, how to think about bumping up against production constraints and confidence in sustaining growth.

Confident — 13 active co-packers with more in discussion, beverage-industry hire Paul Storey, and an internal directive for sales to 'outsell production.' Good position with capacity to drive scale, while acknowledging external factors can happen.
Co-packer pace, can supply & inventory composition

Asked about co-packer pace (now 13) and 2022 domestic expectations, whether domestic can supply has caught up, the inventory mix of cans vs. finished product, the labor/logistics effect on the freight gap, and whether the CycleBar exclusive covers all national CycleBars.

At six orbits, will create more as it scales; in discussions with additional co-packers/warehouses. Can supply remains tight industry-wide but Celsius well positioned via long-term agreements. ~15-20% of inventory is packaging components, the balance finished product plus raw/packaging materials. Outbound-freight gross-profit gap historically ~8-10%, with macro/gas-price uncertainty potentially widening it. The CycleBar exclusive covers the couple-hundred national CycleBars.
Asked how much store-expansion runway is left, the Costco store count and growth plans (vs. ~880 warehouses), and the risk Costco could pull the contract.

Opportunity is twofold — optimizing existing accounts (better placement, more flavors, cold placement for velocity) and convenience-channel runway (~44% ACV, ~56% opportunity left), plus untracked-channel growth. In 561 Costco warehouses. Acknowledged the standard retail dynamic — roughly six months to perform or risk losing the shelf — but Celsius is currently gaining distribution on strong velocity.
